name: 14769-longdecode-deepseekv2lite-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), SM90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, EP off. One in-process vLLM engine, one process, no NCCL.
architecture: MoE decoder, DeepseekV2ForCausalLM: 27 layers (first dense), 64 routed + 2 shared experts, top-6 routing, multi-head latent attention, bf16 -- all in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=[1, 8]. THE OPERATING POINT IS LOAD-BEARING, AND IN THE DOWNWARD DIRECTION: the cost this workload is aimed at is a fixed quantity of HOST time per decode step, which does not shrink with batch, while device time per step grows with it -- so its share is a decreasing function of concurrency and a device-bound point reads ~0 for a real effect. 1 is the scored point (guidellm's first benchmark); 8 is run after it, from the same engine, so the two can be read against each other. max_requests 10 at each stream count -- 10 requests x 1000 forced output tokens is ~10k inter-token samples per benchmark, which pins a median far tighter than the run-to-run floor, while a 1-stream 1000-token generation on this model costs ~23 s of wall clock, so a larger count buys sampling nobody needs and risks the runner's no-progress window; warmup 10% and cooldown 10% both pinned to `requests` mode (with a 1800 s safety cap present, the default `prefer_duration` sizes the cooldown against the CAP, not the run, and swallows the whole measurement window); safety cap 1800 s.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 1000 tokens and output exactly 1000 (min = max), greedy at temperature 0.0, seed 14769; the backend forces ignore_eos, so all 1000 tokens are always generated. `request_format: plain` -- the prompt is sent as raw completion text with no chat template applied, which is both what the source measured and the only format this engine generation's in-process backend can build.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant generating thousand-token drafts from thousand-token briefs for one to eight concurrent users on a single GPU.
launch:
# The engine's arguments. `VLLM_USE_V1=1` must be in the process environment before the engine is
# constructed: at this commit it defaults to 0, there is no CLI flag for it, and without it the V0
# engine is served, which is a different program.
#
# 0.7.3-era AsyncEngineArgs: an unknown key is a TypeError at engine construction, so do not add
# keys from a later vLLM. Every value must stay on ONE top-level line; an indented line is skipped.

model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat

# Required, not decorative: `deepseek_v2` is not a model_type the pinned transformers knows, so
# AutoConfig cannot load this repo's config without it.
trust-remote-code: true

tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 16384
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Pinned rather than left to the default: this engine's per-context default table has no entry for
# an in-process engine, which falls through to 2048 instead of the served 8192.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
